title: Rufaydah al-Aslamiyyah
hookLine: who kept a tent to treat the wounded, remembered by some as a first nurse

lines: A CLOTH PRESSED TO A WOUND.
A NAME IN A FEW LINES.
cards: Sahih al-Bukhari mentions a tent set up in the mosque at Medina, so that the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, could look in on a wounded man from close by. It does not say whose tent it was.

A wounded man had been carried in from the fighting, and someone had to stop the bleeding, change the dressings, sit through the night. Another early source gives that someone a name, in just a few lines.
Today: Rufaydah, from the tribe of Aslam.

teach.h: A TENT IN THE MOSQUE FOR SA'D.
teach.b: The wounded man in Bukhari's report is Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, hit at the battle of the Trench. Bukhari doesn't name who ran the tent.

The early biography of the Prophet by Ibn Ishaq fills that in: the tent belonged to a woman of Aslam named Rufaydah, who treated the wounded, and who gave her own effort to caring for Muslims in need. That's nearly all.
No speeches, no long story. A woman, a tent, and wounds that needed looking after. She wasn't the only woman doing this work.
Bukhari also keeps the words of al-Rubayyi bint Mu'awwidh: the women went out with the Prophet, gave water to the fighters, served them, and carried the wounded and the dead back to Medina.
Rufaydah stands in a line of women who did the unglamorous part. Notice where her tent was. Not at the edge of town, but in the mosque, the center of the community, right where people prayed.

Healing was given a place beside worship, not behind it. Some today call Rufaydah the first nurse of Islam. The old reports say something smaller: she treated the wounded, and the Prophet sent a wounded leader to her.
They never describe the tent itself. They keep who was lying in it, and whose it was.

how: Muslims remember Rufaydah from the early biography of the Prophet, where her tent in the mosque at Medina is where the wounded were cared for.

games.q: you are the Prophet. a leader of Medina is badly wounded. where do you have him cared for?
o: in his own house, across town.
in a tent in the mosque, near you.
games.why: Bukhari says a tent was set up in the mosque so the Prophet could visit him from close by, and Ibn Ishaq says it was Rufaydah's tent.

practice: Bring to mind someone who has cared for a body you love: a nurse, a midwife, a carer, a parent up at three in the morning with a fever, maybe you. See their hands, and let a plain thank you form.
If you pray, you can ask God's mercy for those who tend the sick.

wordCard.voice: Rufaydah al-Aslamiyyah. The woman of Aslam whose tent in Medina was where the wounded were treated. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the name Rufaydah, the woman of Aslam who tended the wounded.

carryVoice: Your line: the tent of healing. Care for the sick, right beside the place of prayer. Day eight hundred forty-eight, done.
